To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the current limiting performance of a 20-MVA superconducting transformer and cable can be enhanced by adjusting the length of the cable, thickness of the stabilizer layer, and critical current of the superconductors.

a 66/3.3 kV–20 MVA REBCO superconductor transformer and cable can limit excess fault currents to triple the rated value after 0.1 s by adjusting the length of superconducting cable and Ic, as well as the thickness of the copper layer.

limiting the excess of fault current to triple of rated current after 200 ms can be achieved by the combination of superconducting transformer and cable by adjusting the thickness and length of stabilizing copper layer and Ic of the superconductings cables.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a superconducting transformer and cable that is capable of limiting an excess current to triple the nominal current after 0,2 s.
the development of a current-limiting superconducting transformer and cable.
a numerical analysis of the current-limiting function of a 20 MVA superconducting transformer and cable.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a 20 M VA REBCO superconductor cable and transformer with a current limiting function could be developed.

the current-limiting function of REBCO cables and transformers is effective for a fault current of 10 times the rated current, but it is not sufficient to limit the current to three times the rated current.
a superconducting transformer can limit the overcurrent of a cable and vice versa, and that the combination of the two is effective for the protection of power systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the superconducting transformer and cable can be used to limit the overcurrent of the superconductors in the transformer and cable, and the superconducting windings in the transformer and the cable can be used as a current-limiting device.
the current-limiting function of a superconducting transformer can be achieved by the cooperation of the superconductivity of the transformer and the cable.

the numerical analysis demonstrated the possibility of limiting the excess fault to triple the rated value after 0.1 s with a 66/10.5 kV, 20 MVA superconducting transformer and cable, while maintaining a superconductivity state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to consider the current limit of a superconducting transformer and cable as a whole system.
it is possible to limit the excess current to triple the rating of the superconductors by optimizing the copper layer of the superconductivity winding of the transformer.
